title: Naturality of the projection formula
statement:
Consider a
cartesian square as in
[def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring,
$E\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$. The
following square commutes:

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
g^{-1}(Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}K)
&\xrightarrow{\;g^{-1}\mathrm{PF}_f\;}&
g^{-1}Rf_*(E\kunotimes{\Lambda}f^{-1}K)\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle \Ex\otimes1}&&
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle \Ex}\\
Rf'_*(g')^{-1}E\kunotimes{\Lambda}g^{-1}K
&\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{PF}_{f'}\;}&
Rf'_*\bigl((g')^{-1}E\kunotimes{\Lambda}(f')^{-1}g^{-1}K\bigr).
\end{array}
$$

Here $\mathrm{PF}$ is the map of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], $\Ex$ is the unbounded exchange of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], and the tensor is [def-kun-derived-tensor]. The canonical monoidal identifications for inverse image are
understood. Thus, whenever the displayed exchange and
projection-formula morphisms are isomorphisms, their inverses satisfy the same compatibility.

proof.text: Use the unbounded derived adjunctions and exchange formula of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], and the projection map of [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Write $L=f^{-1}$, $R=Rf_*$, $L'=f'^{-1}$, $R'=Rf'_*$, $G=g^{-1}$, $H=g'^{-1}$, and $\theta:L'G\to HL$. Write $c^u$ for the inverse of the canonical tensor comparison of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], and suppress these comparisons only after making them. The square identification of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] is monoidal for these canonical comparisons: after identifying the source and target of $\theta_{A\otimes B}$ with tensor products, it is $\theta_A\otimes\theta_B$. Indeed inverse-image composition and its tensor comparison, on a local pure tensor $a\otimes b$, send it to the pair of pulled-back labels; either order of composition gives the same pair. The sheafification universal property makes these bilinear rules equal on sheaves. On K-flat flat-term models the same equality holds in every bidegree of the total tensor, with the same differential signs in both routes. The canonical derived comparisons are these comparisons on those models; uniqueness of extension in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] makes the equality hold on all derived objects. This checks tensor compatibility explicitly, rather than inferring it from compatibility with pasted squares alone.

source.place: ## Proof: explicit expansion of the common-mate calculation, step 1

proof.text:
Put $M=RE\otimes K$, $N=E\otimes LK$, $B=HE\otimes L'GK$, and $\rho=1_{HE}\otimes\theta_K^{-1}:HN\to B$, using the tensor comparisons of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal]. From [def-kun-projection-formula-map] put $a=(\varepsilon_{f,E}\otimes1)c^f_{RE,K}:LM\to N$, so $\varepsilon_{f,N}L(\mathrm{PF}_f)=a$. From [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], put $\beta_A=H(\varepsilon_{f,A})\theta_{RA}$, so $\varepsilon_{f',HA}L'(\Ex_A)=\beta_A$. The transpose under $L'\dashv R'$ of the top-then-right route $R'\rho\circ\Ex_N\circ G(\mathrm{PF}_f)$ is
$$\rho\,\beta_N\,L'G(\mathrm{PF}_f)=\rho\,H(\varepsilon_{f,N})\,HL(\mathrm{PF}_f)\,\theta_M=\rho\,H(a)\,\theta_M.$$
The first equality is the defining exchange transpose and naturality of the counit for $\rho$; the second is naturality of $\theta$ for $\mathrm{PF}_f$; the third is the defining projection transpose. No exchange map is assumed invertible.

source.place: ## Proof: explicit expansion of the common-mate calculation, step 2

proof.text:
Identify $GM$ with $GRE\otimes GK$ by [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal]. By [def-kun-projection-formula-map], the transpose of the left-then-bottom route is
$$(\varepsilon_{f',HE}\otimes1)c^{f'}_{R'HE,GK}L'(\Ex_E\otimes1)=(\varepsilon_{f',HE}L'\Ex_E\otimes1)c^{f'}_{GRE,GK}=(\beta_E\otimes1)c^{f'}_{GRE,GK}.$$
Here the middle equality is bifunctoriality of the tensor comparison and the final equality is the exchange transpose in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. The expression from step 2 is the same morphism: expand $a$, use tensor compatibility of $\theta$ from step 1 and naturality of the comparison for $H$, and obtain $(H\varepsilon_{f,E}\theta_{RE})\otimes(\theta_K^{-1}\theta_K)$ after the source comparison. The second factor is the identity, leaving $(\beta_E\otimes1)c^{f'}_{GRE,GK}$.

source.place: ## Proof: explicit expansion of the common-mate calculation, step 3

proof.text: The adjunction Hom bijection of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] is injective. The equal transposes in steps 2 and 3 therefore give commutativity of the displayed square. For its four arrows write $a$ for the top, $b$ for the bottom, $u$ for the left and $v$ for the right; the equality is $va=bu$. When all four arrows are invertible, multiplying by inverses gives $a^{-1}v^{-1}=u^{-1}b^{-1}$, the commutativity of the reversed square.

lemma rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap_derivedBaseChangeMap (sq : CommSq g' f' f g)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A))
    (L : DerivedCategory (Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology A)) :
    L((g)^*[A]).map (((rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap A f).app K).app L) ≫
        (derivedBaseChangeMap A sq).app (((-⊗ᴸ-(X)[A]).obj K).obj (L((f)^*[A]).obj L)) ≫
        R((f')_*[A]).map (((leftDerivedUpperStarTensorComparison A g').app K).app
          (L((f)^*[A]).obj L)) =
      ((leftDerivedUpperStarTensorComparison A g).app (R((f)_*[A]).obj K)).app L ≫
        ((-⊗ᴸ-(Y')[A]).map ((derivedBaseChangeMap A sq).app K)).app (L((g)^*[A]).obj L) ≫
        ((rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap A f').app (L((g')^*[A]).obj K)).app
          (L((g)^*[A]).obj L) ≫
        R((f')_*[A]).map (((-⊗ᴸ-(X')[A]).obj (L((g')^*[A]).obj K)).map
          ((derivedSquareUpperStarIso A sq).hom.app L))

This is the displayed square with its canonical monoidal identifications written out: postcompose the equality by Rf'_*(1 ⊗ theta_K.inv) to put its common target in the displayed bottom-right presentation. The left-derived inverse images and derivedBaseChangeMap are the exact inverse images and exactDerivedBaseChangeMap of the recorded exchange transported along leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory: mapDerivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction_eq identifies the adjunctions, and leftDerivedUpperStarComp is the descended ordinary composition comparison through the same exactness isomorphisms. Projection and tensor are precisely the declarations recorded by def-kun-projection-formula-map and def-kun-derived-tensor. The inverse compatibility is the reversed-isomorphism square (CommSq.vert_inv followed by CommSq.horiz_inv). No boundedness, properness, coefficient finiteness, torsion, or invertibility assumption is needed for the forward equality.
